info.title: Tuteliq API
info.description:
# AI-Powered Child Safety API

You're building a chat feature for a kids' learning app. A user sends a message that looks innocuous on the surface but contains subtle grooming escalation patterns. Tuteliq catches it, scores the risk by the child's age group, and gives your trust & safety team an actionable report, typically in about a second, or around 400ms in fast mode on a dedicated deployment. One API call replaces months of in-house ML work.

---

## KOSA Harm Categories Coverage

| Harm Category | Endpoint | Status |
|--------------|----------|--------|
| Eating Disorders | `/safety/unsafe` | ✅ Covered |
| Substance Use | `/safety/unsafe` | ✅ Covered |
| Suicidal Behaviors | `/safety/unsafe` | ✅ Covered |
| Depression & Anxiety | `/safety/unsafe` + `/analysis/emotions` | ✅ Covered |
| Compulsive Usage | `/safety/unsafe` | ✅ Covered |
| Harassment & Bullying | `/safety/bullying` | ✅ Covered |
| Sexual Exploitation | `/safety/grooming` + `/safety/unsafe` | ✅ Covered |
| Voice & Audio Threats | `/safety/voice` | ✅ Covered |
| Visual Content Risks | `/safety/image` | ✅ Covered |

---

## Key Features

- **Age-Calibrated Severity** — Risk scores adjust across four age brackets (under 10, 10–12, 13–15, 16–17) so moderation matches developmental context.

- **Nuanced Context Recognition** — Distinguishes hyperbolic teen language from genuine crisis signals, dramatically reducing false positives.

- **Grooming Pattern Detection** — Identifies multi-stage grooming tactics: trust escalation, secrecy requests, isolation attempts, and boundary violations.

- **Emotional Trend Analysis** — Tracks persistent mood patterns across conversations to surface early indicators of declining mental health.

- **Voice & Image Analysis** — Upload audio or images for transcription, OCR, and full safety analysis in a single call.

- **Real-time Voice Streaming** — WebSocket endpoint for live audio moderation with configurable flush intervals and per-category alerts.

- **Guidance & Reports** — Generate age-appropriate action plans and professional incident reports ready for handoff to human reviewers.

- **Batch Processing & Webhooks** — Analyze up to 50 items per batch call, with HMAC-signed webhook alerts for critical incidents.

---

## Credits per Action

| Endpoint | Credits | Notes |
|----------|---------|-------|
| `detectBullying` | 1 | Single text analysis |
| `detectUnsafe` | 1 | Single text analysis |
| `detectGrooming` | 1 per 10 msgs | `ceil(messages / 10)`, min 1 |
| `analyzeEmotions` | 1 per 10 msgs | `ceil(messages / 10)`, min 1 |
| `getActionPlan` | 2 | Longer generation |
| `generateReport` | 3 | Structured output |
| `analyzeVoice` | 5 | Transcription + analysis |
| `analyzeImage` | 3 | Vision + OCR + analysis |

Every response includes a `credits_used` field. Credit balance is also available via the `X-Credits-Remaining` response header.

---

## Quick Start

**1.** Get your API key at [tuteliq.ai/dashboard](https://tuteliq.ai/dashboard)

**2.** Install the SDK:

```bash
npm install @tuteliq/sdk
```

**3.** Make your first call:

```typescript
import Tuteliq from '@tuteliq/sdk'

const tuteliq = new Tuteliq({ apiKey: 'YOUR_API_KEY' })

const result = await tuteliq.detectUnsafe({
  content: "Don't talk to your parents about us meeting up",
  context: { age_group: "13-15" }
})

console.log(result.unsafe)              // true
console.log(result.categories)          // ["grooming_adjacent", "secrecy"]
console.log(result.severity)            // "high"
console.log(result.recommended_action)  // "Escalate to moderator"
```

---

## Performance

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Full detection, shared tier | ~1.4s typical |
| Fast mode (`verdict_only`), shared tier | ~1.0s typical |
| Fast mode, dedicated deployment | ~400ms |
| Uptime SLA | 99.9% |

Shared-tier figures are what a standard API key sees today. The dedicated figure is
the same model served on reserved hardware without the shared-tier hop, and is
available on enterprise plans rather than by default.

Check real-time status at [tuteliq.ai/status](https://tuteliq.ai/status)

get.summary: Get the customer-registered public key for end-to-end incident encryption
get.description: Returns the public key currently used to encrypt incident records, or 404 if none is registered. When no key is registered, incidents fall back to server-side encryption (Tuteliq holds the key). Register a public key with POST to switch to true end-to-end encryption — only your dashboard can decrypt.

post.summary: Register (or rotate) the public key Tuteliq uses to encrypt your incident records
post.description:
Registers an RSA public key. After registration, all NEW incident records (rationale, visual_description, etc.) are encrypted with a per-record AES key, which is itself wrapped with this RSA key (hybrid scheme RSA-OAEP + AES-256-GCM). Tuteliq cannot decrypt — only your dashboard (with the matching private key) can.

Rotating: POST a new key here. New incidents use the new key; old incidents remain readable with the old private key until they expire (90 days).

Private key is YOUR responsibility — Tuteliq cannot recover lost-key incidents.

algorithm.description: RSA-OAEP key size. 2048-bit is faster, 4096-bit is more conservative.

public_key_pem.description: PEM-encoded SPKI public key (begins with "-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----").

delete.description: After revocation, new incidents fall back to server-side encryption (Tuteliq holds the key). Existing incidents stay encrypted under the previous key and remain readable only with its private key. Common reason to revoke: key compromise (then immediately register a new one).

post.summary: Validate and process a document image via session (mobile)
post.description: Per-step document validation for the cross-device flow. Checks image quality, then runs the document work (text extraction, face template) so that the submit step does not need the document image again: the session carries the result, never the image, until the session is submitted, cancelled, or expires. Send `side` (`front`, `back` or `passport`) and `document_type` as form fields ahead of the file. `retained: false` means the document was not held (encryption unavailable, or the document could not be processed) and must be included in the submit. Free, no credits consumed.

post.summary: Validate and assess a selfie via session (mobile)
post.description: Per-step selfie validation for the cross-device flow. Always checks that a face is present. When the request also carries the liveness capture (`liveness_frame` files and the `liveness_token` field), it runs the selfie assessment now (liveness, age estimation, and the face match against the document already processed by validate-document) and the session carries the DECISION, never the selfie or the frames, to submit, which then needs no images. `assessed: false` means the assessment did not run (no capture sent, or nothing to match against) and the submit must carry the selfie and liveness as before. Free, no credits consumed.

Complete a verification using a session token. When validate-document and validate-selfie already processed the document and the selfie for this session, this request needs no images at all and returns immediately. Otherwise send the selfie and liveness capture (and, unless validate-document processed them, the ID document images). Images included in this request always take precedence over what the session carries.

post.summary: Report verification step progress from mobile
post.description: Used by mobile device to report which step the user is on, so desktop can show real-time progress.

get.summary: Which document sides the session already holds a processed result for
get.description: Session-token authenticated. Used by a device that resumed past the document steps while the other device was still reading the document: it polls this until the sides it needs are held, then continues without capturing the document again. Never returns document content.

get.summary: Resolve verification mode and language for end-user
get.description: Called by the HTML verification page on load. Detects the end-user country from IP, resolves the verification mode from market config, and returns the UI language. No authentication required — session ID is unguessable (128-bit entropy).

get.summary: Subscribe to session status updates via SSE
get.description: Server-Sent Events stream that emits status changes and results for a verification session. No authentication required — session ID is unguessable (128-bit entropy).

post.summary: Detect bullying, harassment, and intimidation in text
post.description: Analyze a message for bullying indicators including verbal abuse, social exclusion, threats, and cyberbullying patterns. Returns severity (low/medium/high/critical), bullying type classification, confidence score, and a recommended action. Risk scores are age-calibrated when context.ageGroup is provided.

language.description: Language code (e.g., "en"). 27 supported languages: en is stable, the other 26 are beta (es, pt, uk, sv, no, da, fi, de, fr, nl, pl, it, tr, ro, el, cs, hu, bg, hr, sk, lt, lv, et, sl, mt, ga). Auto-detected if omitted.

support_threshold.description: Minimum severity to show crisis support resources (default: high). Critical always shows.

verdict_only.description: Fast mode: skip generating `action_detail`, the moderator-guidance expansion of `recommended_action`. Lower latency and a smaller response; `rationale` (used for incident summaries) and the verdict itself (severity, categories, recommended_action, risk_score) are unchanged.

flag_profanity.description: Additive, deterministic word-list flag for plain profanity/vulgarity. Adds `profanity` to the response; never affects `is_bullying`, `severity`, `risk_score`, or `recommended_action`. Free — no extra credits. Not a harm classifier: does not cover slurs or hate speech, which the detector itself already handles with full context.

flag_risk_terms.description: Additive, deterministic word-list flag for bare drug and violence terms (e.g. "cocaine", "kill"). Adds `risk_terms` to the response; never affects `is_bullying`, `severity`, `risk_score`, or `recommended_action`. Free — no extra credits. Purely lexical: WILL fire on benign uses of an included term ("kill the lights") since it cannot read context the way the detector itself does — combine with the detector’s own verdict for a stricter policy, don’t use in isolation as a block decision.

support_threshold.description: Top-level alias for options.support_threshold. Minimum severity to show crisis support resources (default: high). Critical always shows.

continuation_token.description: Opaque signed token from a previous /bullying call. Carries derived analysis state — no message content is stored server-side.

reset_conversation.description: Discard any continuation_token and start a fresh conversation.

message_id.description: Optional customer-side message id for evidence pointers.

external_id.description: Your unique identifier (e.g. message ID, content ID) for correlating Tuteliq results with your own system. Echoed back in the response and included in webhook payloads so you can match alerts to the original content.

customer_id.description: Your end-customer identifier for multi-tenant / B2B2C scenarios. If you serve multiple customers (schools, apps, brands) from a single API key, set this to route webhook alerts to the correct customer. Echoed back in the response and included in webhook payloads as "customerId".

metadata.description: Arbitrary key-value pairs for additional context (e.g. { "channel": "discord", "region": "eu" }). Stored with the detection result, echoed in the response, and included in webhook payloads. Maximum 20 properties.

incident_moderation_enabled.description: Per-call override of your account incident logging setting. When set, it takes precedence over the account-level flag for THIS request: true forces the incident to be persisted, false suppresses persistence. Omit to use your account default (which itself defaults to enabled). Lets you control incident logging per request, e.g. suppress logging for test traffic.

speaker_role.description: The speaker's relationship to the conduct described, so a report can be routed to a victim-protection queue rather than a sender-sanction one without parsing rationale prose. `enacting` = the speaker is bullying. `experiencing` = the speaker describes what was done to them. `reporting_other` = a bystander describing a third party's conduct, or relaying someone else's decision. `self_directed` = the speaker disparages only themselves. `unclear` = cannot be determined. Descriptive: this never changes `is_bullying`, `severity`, `risk_score` or `recommended_action`. It is the ONLY field that distinguishes the person bullying from the person being bullied, since `is_bullying` reports presence for both. Same vocabulary as `speaker_role` on /safety/coercive-control.

is_bullying.description: Whether a bullying signal is PRESENT in the content, at ANY severity (including low / monitor cases). Presence, not authorship: this is `true` for a child describing bullying being done TO them, exactly as it is for the person doing it. Use `speaker_role` to tell those apart before you act on it, or you will sanction the victim. For production branching prefer `recommended_action` (`flag_for_review` / `block` / `immediate_intervention`), which is a stable enum, over the bare presence of a signal.

bullying_type.description: Canonical vocabulary. Values outside this enum are dropped before the response is built, so this field is safe to switch on.

recommended_action.description: Routing key, weakest to strongest: `none`, `monitor`, `flag_for_review`, `block`, `immediate_intervention`. Safe to switch on.

action_detail.description: Optional human-readable expansion of `recommended_action` for a moderator UI. Free text: do not branch on it.

language.description: Language code used for analysis (auto-detected or provided)

credits_used.description: Number of credits consumed by this request

continuation_token.description: Signed token carrying derived analysis state for the next call. Server stores nothing.

continuation_expires_at.description: ISO 8601 expiry timestamp of the continuation_token.

trajectory_risk.description: Conversation-level risk 0-1, distinct from `risk_score` which scores only this message. Anchored on the highest severity seen so far and decaying slowly across benign turns, so a friendly message after an escalation does not reset it. Absent on the first turn. Derived from the signed token: no message content is stored to produce it.

trajectory.description: Direction of travel across the conversation so far.

severity_series.description: Per-turn severity, oldest first — the evidence behind `trajectory_risk`, so a moderator can see why a benign-looking message carries elevated conversation risk.

escalation_capped.description: True when a coded-term match pushed severity toward critical but this endpoint's corroboration-cap logic held recommended_action below immediate_intervention pending independent confirmation. Absent when no cap applied.

escalation_capped_reason.description: Human-readable explanation of the cap. Present only when escalation_capped is true.

profanity.description: Present only when options.flag_profanity (or the account-level default_flag_profanity setting) is true. Deterministic word-list result — additive, never affects is_bullying/severity/risk_score/recommended_action.

risk_terms.description: Present only when options.flag_risk_terms (or the account-level default_flag_risk_terms setting) is true. Deterministic drug/violence word-list result — additive, never affects is_bullying/severity/risk_score/recommended_action. Purely lexical: can fire on benign uses of an included term.

external_id.description: Echo of the external_id you provided in the request

customer_id.description: Echo of the customer_id you provided in the request

metadata.description: Echo of the metadata you provided in the request

support.description: Country-specific crisis helplines and response guidance (only included for high/critical severity)

post.description: Analyze a sequence of messages for multi-stage grooming tactics: trust building, isolation, secrecy requests, boundary testing, and sexual escalation. Accepts full conversation history with sender roles to detect patterns that single-message analysis would miss. Returns grooming risk level, identified tactics as flags, and recommended intervention actions.

sender_age.description: Optional numeric age of THIS message's sender. Strengthens age-gap analysis without forcing the model to infer it from the role label.

messages.description: Sequence of messages to analyze. Consecutive same-role messages of ≤3 characters are automatically defragmented before tactic analysis to prevent letter-by-letter evasion.

continuation_token.description: Opaque signed token from a previous /grooming call. Carries derived analysis state across calls without server-side storage.

reset_conversation.description: Discard any continuation_token and start a fresh conversation.

message_id.description: Optional customer-side identifier for this batch (used as the evidence pointer in the issued continuation_token).

child_age.description: Age of the child / minor in the conversation.

participant_age.description: Optional age of the non-minor participant. When known (e.g. on age-verified platforms), this lets the model compute the actual age gap rather than infer it.

support_threshold.description: Minimum severity to show crisis support resources (default: high). Critical always shows.

verdict_only.description: Fast mode: omit the per-message `message_analysis` array and `action_detail` from the response, reducing output length and latency. `rationale` (used for incident summaries) is always generated.

support_threshold.description: Top-level alias for options.support_threshold. Minimum severity to show crisis support resources (default: high). Critical always shows.

external_id.description: Your unique identifier (e.g. message ID, content ID) for correlating Tuteliq results with your own system. Echoed back in the response and included in webhook payloads so you can match alerts to the original content.

customer_id.description: Your end-customer identifier for multi-tenant / B2B2C scenarios. If you serve multiple customers (schools, apps, brands) from a single API key, set this to route webhook alerts to the correct customer. Echoed back in the response and included in webhook payloads as "customerId".

metadata.description: Arbitrary key-value pairs for additional context (e.g. { "channel": "discord", "region": "eu" }). Stored with the detection result, echoed in the response, and included in webhook payloads. Maximum 20 properties.

incident_moderation_enabled.description: Per-call override of your account incident logging setting. When set, it takes precedence over the account-level flag for THIS request: true forces the incident to be persisted, false suppresses persistence. Omit to use your account default (which itself defaults to enabled). Lets you control incident logging per request, e.g. suppress logging for test traffic.

conversation_type_applied.description: Present only when a caller-declared `context.conversation_type` actually changed routing. Confirms the setting was taken into account, rather than leaving the platform to assume it was.

grooming_risk.description: Grooming-risk level. "low" indicates a signal worth monitoring but no action required; branch your alerting on `recommended_action` (`flag_for_review` / `block` / `immediate_intervention`), not the bare presence of a low-level risk.

verdict_withdrawn.description: True when the analysis returned a high or critical verdict with no tactic and no risk score to support it. The verdict was reconciled to what the response actually evidences and recommended_action brought down to review, rather than returning two fields that contradict each other. Never fires on a finding that names a tactic or carries any score. Absent unless it applied.

verdict_withdrawn_reason.description: Human-readable explanation. Present only when verdict_withdrawn is true.

verdict_capped.description: True when the analysis returned a high or critical verdict carrying a risk score but naming no tactic to support it. The verdict is capped to medium and recommended_action to flag_for_review, so the conversation still reaches a reviewer rather than routing an escalation a reviewer cannot check; risk_score is capped to the top of the medium band. Never fires on a finding that names a tactic. Only ever lowers, never raises. Absent unless it applied.

verdict_capped_reason.description: Human-readable explanation. Present only when verdict_capped is true.

declared_age_overridden.description: True when the caller declared an adult child_age but a participant states a minor age in the conversation itself. The declared age was not used. Nothing is escalated by this on its own; the analysis simply runs as if no age had been sent. Worth investigating at your end: an age check that disagrees with what the user says in the chat is what a bypassed age verification looks like. A stated ADULT age never has this effect, because message text is attacker-controlled.

declared_age_overridden_reason.description: Human-readable explanation. Present only when declared_age_overridden is true.

flags.description: Closed vocabulary. Values outside this list are dropped before the response is built, so this field is safe to switch on. Two groups share the array. The eight TACTICS the analyser classifies against are `secrecy_request`, `boundary_pushing`, `photo_request`, `gift_giving`, `isolation`, `flattery`, `sexual_content` and `meeting_request`; each asserts that a participant performed that behaviour. The remaining four, `sexualization`, `reconnaissance`, `grooming` and `sextortion`, reach this array from coded-term corroboration and assert something weaker: that the conversation contains a recognised coded term of that kind. If you are reporting on the tactic taxonomy, use the first eight.

confidentiality_frame.description: The adult's own framing of who may know, described factually rather than judged. `unconditional_concealment` asks the child to keep something from someone with no stated limit; `limited_confidentiality` offers privacy but names a condition under which the adult would tell someone ("unless someone's at risk"), which is safeguarding practice rather than a secrecy demand; `guardian_included` tells the child to inform a parent or carer, or says the adult will.

secrecy_frame_cleared.description: True when `secrecy_request` was removed from `flags` because the adult stated the limits of confidentiality or included a guardian. Routing is unaffected: the secrecy_request + isolation escalation reads the pre-removal flag list, so this can never lower an action. Absent when nothing was removed.

flag_attribution.description: Which participant each flag is attributed to: tactic -> the `sender_role` values of the messages that actually carry it. Derived from the per-message analysis, so it answers "who is doing this?" rather than assuming the non-child role. Omitted when the model produced no per-message tags. Attribution only; it does not change the verdict or imply the other party is blameless.

ungrounded_flags.description: Conversation-level tactics the model asserted but that could not be supported: either tied to no specific message at all, or tied only to messages that a separate adjudication check found do not express that tactic (#262). Removed from `flags` and surfaced rather than silently dropped: a tactic here is an UNSUPPORTED claim, not a finding, and should not be treated as evidence.

reciprocity_floor_applied.description: True when the verdict was floored to at least medium / 0.6 / flag_for_review because a separate factual classifier confirmed adult-minor romantic reciprocity - an adult and a minor declaring or reciprocating romantic love, directly or relayed through a third party (#189). A raise-only floor: it never lowers anything, and it exists because this implicit-outcome shape carries no tactic vocabulary and its model-side detection proved unstable across sittings (#292). Absent when the floor did not apply.

consent_floor_applied.description: True when `recommended_action` was raised to `immediate_intervention` because the model reported an explicit refusal being overridden, or a threat to expose an intimate image or a confidence, in order to obtain compliance. This is a floor and never lowers an action. default_flag_profanity.description: Account-level default for options.flag_profanity on /bullying and /unsafe. A request that sets options.flag_profanity explicitly always overrides this.

default_flag_risk_terms.description: Account-level default for options.flag_risk_terms on /bullying and /unsafe. A request that sets options.flag_risk_terms explicitly always overrides this.

delete.description: Remove all custom detection settings. All endpoints will be active.

get.summary: Fetch an EU AI Act Art 12 audit receipt
get.description: Returns the signed audit receipt for a past inference. Only the deployer that produced the receipt can fetch it (api-key fingerprint match enforced; non-matches return 404 to avoid existence leaks). Receipts are signature-verified before return; tampered storage triggers a 500 with code AUDIT_RECEIPT_FAILED.

payload.description: The signed payload. Inputs were not stored — only their hash.

canonical.description: The canonical JSON bytes that were signed (use for out-of-band verification).

post.summary: Submit a moderator review of an incident (Art 14 human oversight)
post.description: Records a deployer-side moderator decision (confirm / downgrade / escalate / reclassify / dismiss) on a model-produced incident. The override is persisted to the incident document and a separate signed Art 12 audit receipt is emitted linking back to the original. The optional reason_comment is encrypted with the customer's registered public key (end-to-end) when enabled; otherwise server-side AES.

post.summary: Submit the same moderator review across multiple incidents (Art 14, bulk)
post.description: Applies the same review action + reason to up to 100 incidents in one call. Each incident emits its own signed Art 12 audit receipt — bulk is a UX shortcut, not a compliance shortcut. Per-incident success/error is returned so a partial failure can be retried without re-running successful items.

get.summary: List the caller's incidents (newest first, paginated)
get.description: Read-only paginated listing of incidents recorded under this API key's account. Each row is non-PII metadata by default; pass `include_summary=true` to include the decrypted incident summary (extra credits per row). BYOK incidents return the hybrid envelope on the summary field and list the field name in `_e2e_envelope_fields`.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Filter by risk_category (e.g. "bullying", "grooming").

parameters.name: severity
parameters.description: Filter by risk_level.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter by status.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Filter by source modality.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: ISO 8601 inclusive lower bound on created_at.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: ISO 8601 exclusive upper bound on created_at.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: 1..100, default 25.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque next_cursor from the previous page.

parameters.name: include_summary
parameters.description: Set "true" to include decrypted summary text on each row (extra credits per row).

get.summary: KPI overview of incidents in a time window
get.description: Counts by category, severity, source, and status, plus top platforms and 24h/7d/30d totals. Defaults to the last 30 days. Read-only; no LLM call.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: ISO 8601 inclusive lower bound; default = now - 30d.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: ISO 8601 exclusive upper bound; default = now.

get.description: Returns time-bucketed counts of incidents (with per-bucket severity breakdown). Bucket sizes: hour, day (default), week. Useful for rendering trend charts in dashboards.

parameters.name: bucket
parameters.description: Bucket size; default = day.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: ISO 8601 inclusive lower bound; default = now - 30d.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: ISO 8601 exclusive upper bound; default = now.

get.summary: Get the full detail for a single incident (read-only)
get.description: Returns the full incident document for the caller's account. Server-encrypted fields (summary, metadata, source_data) are decrypted server-side. BYOK fields are returned as hybrid envelopes for client-side decryption — see `_e2e_envelope_fields` in the response for which to decrypt locally. 404 if the incident does not exist or does not belong to this account.

post.summary: Report a device attestation (endpoint agent check-in)
post.description: The tuteliq-agent CLI evaluates the org's device-safety policy locally and reports the pass/fail result here. One latest-state record is kept per device (upsert, no history). The org is derived from the authenticated API key — any org_id in the body is ignored. No user content is stored; only device posture (policy rule results, versions, platform).

policy_id.description: Identifier of the evaluated policy manifest.

passed.description: True iff every policy rule passed.

rule.description: The evaluated policy rule (posture check — process/file/version/OS). Never contains user content.

detail.description: Human-readable reason the rule failed (omitted on pass).

attested_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the local evaluation.

org_id.description: Ignored — the org is always derived from the API key. Never trusted from the body.

expires_at.description: ISO 8601 expiry (attested_at + 90 days); Firestore TTL reaps the row after this.

get.summary: List the org's device fleet with a compliance summary
get.description: Returns every device's latest attestation for the caller's org (newest first) plus a rollup summary (total / compliant / non-compliant / compliance %). Read-only, deterministic, no LLM. Scoped to the API key's org.

get.summary: Get a single device's latest attestation
get.description: Returns the latest attestation for one device in the caller's org. 404 if the device has never checked in (or belongs to another org).
